builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
summary: DemoFoundry replaces hand-collected real robot demonstrations and manually modeled simulation scenes by using coding agents to generate executable interaction programs in a simulator and a learned video renderer to convert proxy videos into photorealistic, action-aligned observations. It costs access to a physics simulator, existing robot episodes to train the renderer, generative rendering compute, and the engineering effort to orchestrate agents, simulation, and filtering pipelines. It can fail if the renderer introduces visual artifacts inconsistent with the true scene, if agent-written programs produce physically implausible interactions that the automated execution checks miss, or if the sim-to-real gap persists in dynamics even when appearance is corrected.
rationale: The method targets robotics data generation with physics simulators, real robot episodes, and custom video-renderer training, none of which fit a constrained-infrastructure LLM production practice.

claims.statement: DemoFoundry replaces hand-collected real robot demonstrations and manually modeled simulation scenes by using coding agents to generate executable interaction programs in a simulator and a learned video renderer to convert proxy videos into photorealistic, action-aligned observations. It costs access to a physics simulator, existing robot episodes to train the renderer, generative rendering compute, and the engineering effort to orchestrate agents, simulation, and filtering pipelines. It can fail if the renderer introduces visual artifacts inconsistent with the true scene, if agent-written programs produce physically implausible interactions that the automated execution checks miss, or if the sim-to-real gap persists in dynamics even when appearance is corrected.

Policies trained on generated demonstrations outperform raw-simulation training and approach the performance of training on an equal number of real demonstrations; no multiplicative factor is reported.
